summary: This short program stores a list of fish names, rearranges that list into alphabetical order, and displays the result.

lines.text: A list holds several values in one name, kept in the order you write them. "Salmon" appears twice on purpose: lists allow duplicates, and sorting keeps both copies rather than removing one.

The sort method reorders the list in place, meaning it changes fish_types itself and returns nothing. For strings the order is alphabetical, so this is why the list must be reprinted afterwards rather than assigned to a new variable.
Printing a list shows it in bracket form with quotes around each item, which lets you confirm the new order and see the two Salmon entries sitting side by side.
